text: A studio-transmitter programme link carries:
options: programme audio/data from studio to transmitter site
explanation: STPL provides the programme feed between studio and transmitter.

text: A microwave link normally requires:
explanation: Point-to-point microwave links generally depend on LOS propagation and adequate Fresnel clearance.

text: An audio limiter is used mainly to:
explanation: Limiters constrain peak levels and help protect downstream equipment from overload.

text: In an AM transmitter, the modulator changes the:
options: amplitude of the RF carrier according to the audio
explanation: AM varies carrier amplitude in accordance with the modulating signal.

text: A dummy load is connected to a transmitter to:
options: provide a known non-radiating load for testing
explanation: A dummy load absorbs RF power so transmitter tests can be performed without radiating.

text: DSB in AM means:
explanation: DSB transmission contains both upper and lower sidebands.

text: PWM stands for:
explanation: PWM varies pulse width according to the modulating/control signal.

text: For ideal AM with carrier, increasing modulation depth primarily increases:
explanation: The sidebands carry the information and their power rises with modulation index.

text: An ATU is used mainly for:
explanation: An Antenna Tuning Unit transforms the antenna impedance toward the required feeder/transmitter impedance.

text: Characteristic impedance of a lossless line is determined by:
options: its distributed inductance and capacitance per unit length
explanation: For a lossless line, Z0=sqrt(L/C).

text: VSWR=1 indicates:
explanation: A VSWR of 1 corresponds to reflection coefficient magnitude zero.

text: Return loss is related to:
explanation: Return loss is -20 log10|Γ|; larger return loss indicates better matching.

text: A quarter-wave line can be used to:
options: convert AC to DC without components
explanation: A λ/4 line provides impedance transformation depending on its characteristic impedance and termination.

text: A Smith chart is primarily used for:
explanation: It graphically handles complex impedances, reflection coefficients and matching.

text: Directional AM arrays use multiple radiators mainly to:
explanation: Relative amplitudes/phases of array elements produce desired azimuthal radiation.

text: Earth radials at an MW transmitting site help:
options: provide a low-loss RF return path near the ground
explanation: A radial ground system reduces ground losses for vertically polarized MW radiation.

text: FM conveys information by varying the carrier's:
explanation: Frequency modulation varies instantaneous frequency according to the message.

text: A common FM broadcast antenna is a:
explanation: FM broadcast stations use VHF antenna arrays such as dipoles/panels.

text: An RF combiner is used to:
options: combine RF power from multiple transmitters/channels
explanation: Combiners combine RF outputs while maintaining controlled impedance and isolation.

text: A directional coupler is used to:
options: sample a known fraction of travelling RF power
explanation: Directional couplers provide a coupled sample with defined coupling/directivity.

text: A diplexer generally allows:
options: two frequency bands/channels to share a common antenna path
DC and AC to short together
two batteries to be paralleled without protection
explanation: A diplexer combines/separates two frequency bands with isolation.

text: A feeder dehydrator is used to:
explanation: Dry air/nitrogen pressurization prevents moisture entering RF feeder systems.

text: In a three-phase system, load balancing aims to:
options: reduce phase imbalance and neutral/feeder stress
explanation: Balanced loading improves system performance and reduces unwanted current imbalance.

text: A UPS primarily provides:
explanation: A UPS bridges mains interruptions and can provide conditioned power to critical loads.

text: Equipment earthing primarily provides:
options: a low-impedance fault path for safety
explanation: Protective earthing helps fault current operate protective devices and limits touch voltage.

text: Sound pressure level is commonly expressed in:
explanation: Sound pressure level is referenced to 20 µPa and expressed in dB SPL.

text: A condenser microphone normally requires:
explanation: Condenser microphones use an electrically biased capsule and internal electronics; many use phantom power.

text: A cardioid microphone has maximum sensitivity primarily:
explanation: Cardioid polar response favours sound arriving from the front and rejects much of the rear.

text: Standard phantom power for many studio condenser microphones is:
explanation: 48 V phantom power is a common professional microphone powering standard.

text: A loudspeaker converts:
explanation: The loudspeaker's transducer converts electrical signal into diaphragm motion and sound.

text: A DAW primarily provides:
explanation: Digital Audio Workstations handle recording, editing, mixing and playback.

text: Lossy audio compression:
options: discards information judged less perceptually important
explanation: Lossy codecs reduce bitrate by removing or approximating perceptually less important information.

text: Reverberation time is commonly defined using:
options: the time for sound level to decay by 60 dB
the time for RF to travel 1 km
explanation: RT60 is the time required for a 60 dB decay after the source stops.

text: A mixer channel typically provides:
explanation: A mixing console controls gain/level, routing, EQ and other audio functions.

text: An OB van is designed primarily for:
explanation: OB facilities provide mobile production for outdoor events.

text: A superheterodyne receiver uses a local oscillator and mixer to create:
explanation: The mixer converts the received RF to a fixed IF for selective amplification/demodulation.

text: An envelope detector is suitable for:
explanation: The envelope contains the AM message when the carrier is sufficiently large and the modulation is appropriate.

text: The discriminator in an FM receiver converts:
explanation: FM discriminators produce an output proportional to instantaneous frequency deviation.

text: THD measures:
options: harmonic distortion relative to the desired signal
explanation: Total Harmonic Distortion quantifies unwanted harmonics relative to the fundamental/reference signal.

text: A VIM is associated with measurement of:
explanation: A Vector Impedance Meter measures impedance magnitude and phase-related parameters.

text: SCPC means:
explanation: SCPC allocates a dedicated carrier to a single channel.

text: MCPC means:
explanation: MCPC multiplexes multiple programme channels onto one carrier.

text: Link budget accounts for:
options: gains and losses from transmitter to receiver
explanation: A link budget sums transmit power, antenna gains, propagation losses and other gains/losses.

text: Look angles from an earth station describe:
explanation: Look angles determine where the earth-station antenna must point.

text: An HPA in an earth station is a:
explanation: The HPA amplifies the uplink RF signal to the required transmit power.

text: Frequency response of an audio chain describes:
options: variation of RF power with tower height
explanation: Frequency response shows how the system gain changes across the audio frequency range.

text: A phone-in system in broadcasting is intended to:
options: interface telephone callers with the studio audio chain
explanation: Phone-in equipment interfaces telephone audio to the studio console with suitable isolation and level control.

text: An IRD at a satellite receiving terminal is used to:
explanation: An Integrated Receiver Decoder recovers the transport/programme streams from the satellite signal.

text: The purpose of an audio equalizer in a transmitter input chain is to:
options: shape frequency response of the programme signal
explanation: An equalizer shapes spectral response to meet the required transmission characteristic.

text: A voltage stabilizer at a transmitting station is used primarily to:
options: maintain supply voltage within an acceptable range
explanation: A stabilizer regulates variations in supply voltage for connected equipment.
